# Protection of Human Subjects

<!-- Required if the project involves human subjects. Much of this is entered
     structurally in the PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information
     form rather than as a narrative attachment — check your NOFO and the
     ASSIST form before writing prose here. Delete this section entirely if
     the project has no human subjects; do not submit an empty attachment. -->

## Risks to Human Subjects

### Human Subjects Involvement, Characteristics, and Design

Population, sample size and its justification, inclusion/exclusion criteria,
and recruitment.

### Sources of Materials

Data and biospecimens to be obtained, and whether they are identifiable.

### Potential Risks

Physical, psychological, social, legal, and privacy risks, and their
likelihood and seriousness.

## Adequacy of Protection Against Risks

### Informed Consent and Assent

Process, or justification for a waiver.

### Protections Against Risk

Safeguards, confidentiality, and data security.

## Potential Benefits to Subjects and Others

Benefits, and why risks are reasonable relative to them.

## Importance of the Knowledge to be Gained

Why the knowledge is worth the risk.

## Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Individuals Across the Lifespan

Planned distribution and its scientific justification.
